title: Which Recurring Tasks Make Business Owners Nervous?
summary: The second-guessing after you hit submit on payroll? You’re not alone. Here’s how to build a system that lets you relax.
body_markdown:
Ask yourself: what parts of your business make you most nervous?


If you’re feeling skeptical, that’s natural. “Of course! The accounting firm is about to talk about how accounting makes people anxious…”


But the question[came up last month](https://www.reddit.com/r/smallbusiness/comments/1ubvdqp/what_recurring_task_makes_you_nervous_every_month/) in r/smallbusiness, one of the most popular online forums for entrepreneurs, and over and over, people answered the same way.


Payroll. Tax. Financial reporting. In that order.


But why?


## **Do You See Yourself In These Responses?**


Over 350,000 people visit r/smallbusiness every week. And last month, one of the most popular posts asked:[What recurring tasks make you nervous?](https://www.reddit.com/r/smallbusiness/comments/1ubvdqp/what_recurring_task_makes_you_nervous_every_month/)


Here’s a snapshot:


- *“Payroll. After I hit submit, my brain starts inventing problems that don’t exist.”*


- *“Anything tied to money leaving on a deadline. Quarterly tax especially.”*


- *“Sales tax never feels casual to me. The task itself is boring, but one wrong mapping or missed deadline can turn into a whole afternoon of second-guessing.”*


Something curious is happening here…


Different people, running different businesses, all said they’re nervous about the same things, in nearly the same words.


## **Your Anxiety Serves a Purpose**


Nervousness is a remarkably accurate readout of where the stakes are highest.


One transposed number in payroll, and you could accidentally drain your cash reserves. Miscode a sales tax map, and your afternoon disappears trying to figure out what happened. Make a quarterly tax estimate that’s off, and you’re either loaning the government money interest-free or bracing for a penalty you didn’t see coming.


There’s a temptation to think the solution is to care less. Or get enough experience that the nerves go away on their own.


But look closely at the thread, and one comment highlights where that goes wrong.


*“Discomfort keeps you sharp. People who stop feeling that low-level anxiety about high-stakes tasks are the ones who eventually let something slip.”*


Everyone in that thread is conscientious. They take the work seriously, check things twice, and catch mistakes. And they’re not anxious because they’re disorganized, or bad with numbers, or not cut for entrepreneurship.


The issue is carrying that high-stakes work with no real support


## **Things That Make You Anxious Are Your Guide**


Vigilance is important. It keeps you safe.


But you only have so much time in a day.


After all, a morning spent reviewing payroll is a morning you could’ve spent growing the business. Right?


It’s hard to always be the second set of eyes. The reconciliation step. The review process. Everything runs through your attention, and can fray your nerves.


It’s fragile, too, because without backup, what happens when you’re overwhelmed? Or sick? Or just human?


The actual solution isn’t to care less. It’s to identify where you need help, and build a system that earns you the right to exhale after you hit submit.

With our managed payroll services, expert controllers review everything, and not just when something looks off. Hours get verified, numbers get a second set of eyes before paychecks are released, and the post-submission anxiety has somewhere to land besides your own head.


*“Sales tax never feels casual. One wrong mapping and there goes my afternoon.”*
